commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-integrated dev server as a new `dev-server.ts` module reusing the existing `buildSite`/`BuildOptions` contract and CLI `run()` flow.

compounding_issues: Session 2 added templating (Handlebars + EJS) into the already monolithic src/generator.ts, growing it to ~187 lines with coupled renderer/partial/registration logic; Session 4 had to pay down this debt with a full plugin refactor

Session 3's dev server was deeply coupled to buildSite(); Session 4's refactor had to rewire it into a DevServerPlugin, leaving an awkward reverse dependency (dev-server.ts imports buildSite from generator.ts while generator's TemplatePlugin emits the index that the server serves)

Session 4 introduced a runtime require/require.extensions TS transpile-loader hack to load ssg.config.ts and plugin modules — functional but a fragile Node-CommonJS idiom that constrains future ESM adoption

The seed codebase (Express Todo API, index.ts) was discarded wholesale in Session 1 — sensible given the prompt mismatch, but it meant the story never exercised incremental evolution of existing code, only greenfield accretion

Session 5's incremental-cache logic (delete-stale loop, cache short-circuiting of plugin onFile hooks) was committed without test verification — the agent's `npm test` and `npm run build` both returned exit 127 ('npm: command not found') and it still committed
key_decisions: Session 1: greenfield TypeScript rewrite discarding the unrelated Express seed — clean baseline, strict tsconfig, Jest + ts-jest harness
Session 2: dual-engine template system (Handlebars + EJS) with partials, layouts, and per-page frontmatter template selection
Session 3: in-process dev server with chokidar file watching and WebSocket live-reload, path-traversal-guarded static serving

Session 4: decomposition into a plugin pipeline (MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin, DevServerPlugin) with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and an emitFile virtual-output model — the pivotal architectural choice
Session 5: content-addressed incremental cache (.ssg-cache.json manifest) keyed by source/template SHA-256 hashes with a getLastBuildStats() CLI report
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 delivered a small, clean, well-typed markdown-to-HTML generator with working CLI and tests. Session 2 expanded capability (templating) but at the cost of a growing monolith. Session 3 integrated a featureful dev server but deepened coupling to buildSite. Session 4 was the arc's peak: a disciplined refactor into a plugin architecture with explicit lifecycle hooks that reduced generator.ts from ~187 to ~87 lines and moved each concern into a focused module with better test coverage. Session 5 added a sophisticated incremental cache and build stats, but grew generator.ts back to ~169 lines, added a runtime require-loader, and — critically — was committed without ever running the test suite (npm was missing from the runtime environment), so the caching hot path went unverified. Overall the system became more modular and extensible at each step, with the only regression risk concentrated in the unverified Session 5 cache logic.
story_review.summary: A coherent, genuinely progressive five-session build where each session layered naturally on the last, peaking in Session 4's plugin refactor, but the unverified, complexity-heavy incremental cache in Session 5 is the one decision that could undermine the prior gains.
